text:
maria: Heads-up — we had a weird flurry of WS resume floods during a routing weight rebalance this morning. A few tenants showed repeated resume attempts and immediate replays; quota flagged them twice. Noticed in eu-central.

chris: saw the spike. it was correlated with a routing roll that changed shard affinity (weight flip) at 03:42 UTC. clients resumed to the old edge, got bounced, then retried to new edge -> duplicate work.

joel: digging into traces: resume_id accepted on proxy A, proxy A lost session after weight change, proxy B rejected resume as mismatch and told client to full reconnect. clients did full reconnects and re-sent requests, which counted again against per-minute quotas.

priya: that's the billing problem we've feared. The routing change should have used a graceful handoff: drain / handover before moving weight. Did the rollout set drain=false?

chris: yes, the rollout used fast weight flip (flag=fast_rebalance). Ops wanted quick rebalance for hot-tenant mitigation.

maria: we need a short-term mitigation: when a routing-change event occurs for a shard, mark sessions for a 20s "handoff mode" where resume acceptance is permissive but quota is suppressed for suspected handoff connections. Pseudocode:
```
on routing_change(shard):
  for session in shard.active:
    session.handoff_mode = true
    set_timer(20s, session.handoff_mode = false)
```

joel: implementable in control-plane; proxy can emit `handoff=1` in resume response so runtime quota knows to skip counting this resume as a new completion request if it replays within 30s.

priya: we should also add telemetry: `ws_handoff_events.v1` and `ws_resume_doublecount.v1`. Dashboard panel: handoff events by route, and a rate of resumed-but-replayed requests hitting quota.

metrics-bot: emit: ws_handoff_events=27 (last 6h), ws_resume_doublecount=14 (last 6h). top routes: /v1/chat=9, /v1/complete=5.

chris: rollout UX: 1) add handoff-mode flag to control-plane API (feature flag), 2) proxy to include handoff header on resume responses when control-plane marks shard, 3) quota estimator to ignore completion count for resumes tagged handoff within 30s, 4) canary on small shard group in eu-central for 12h.

maria: agree. include a dashboard alert: if ws_resume_doublecount > 20/10m then page eng-platform.

joel: note: this is best-effort — if a malicious client replays intentionally during handoff we could undercount. But most replays are legitimate due to transient routing. tradeoff seems acceptable short-term. We'll follow with strict handover protocol (drain + session migration) next quarter.

priya: small thing — ensure that the handoff header doesn't bypass existing billing safeguards for enterprise tenants who opt-out. we'll need an allowlist.

chris: good call. control-plane will check tenant.allowlist for handoff-suppression. default: on for all non-enterprise.

maria: I'll open the dashboard ticket and add the alert. can someone own the quota change PR? @joel?

joel: taking it. will open PRs for control-plane flag + proxy header + quota tweak. linking when ready.

ops-bot: Created ticket: CP-8382 (handoff-mode) and Alert rule 'WS Resume Doublecount Surge' (threshold=20/10m) -> #eng-platform-oncall.

metrics-bot: created dashboard panel 'WS Handoff & Resume Doublecount' in eng-platform/dashboards/streaming.

maria: timeline: PRs today, canary eu-central tomorrow 04:00 UTC, evaluate 12h. rollback: flip control-plane flag off. include steps to force flush handoff markers.

chris: also add a one-off client guidance note in the public status doc: advise customers to implement exponential backoff and treat resume rejections as non-chargeable for 15s if repeated. billing team needs to sign off.

priya: putting billing on the thread. billing: please review allowlist and customer comms.

joel: PR opened: https://git.internal/r/redwood/control-plane/pulls/5412 (handoff-mode flag), https://git.internal/r/redwood/proxy/pulls/2208 (handoff header), https://git.internal/r/redwood/quota/pulls/1407 (ignore-handoff-resume). Reviews welcome.

maria: thanks. reviewing now. :thumbsup:

chris: ack

priya: ack
